meta.titre: Organic Nutrients: carbohydrates, fats and proteins from elements to uses
meta.sous_theme: Composition, functions and sources of carbohydrates, fats and proteins

sections.contenu_markdown:
At a family meal in Bafoussam, there is boiled cassava, plantain, palm oil in the sauce and beans. A nutrition officer says that the meal contains all three organic nutrients.
Carbohydrates, fats and proteins are made by living things from a few chemical elements, and each has its own job in the body.
The GCE examiners ask you to state their composition, their uses and the fate of the food made by green plants, so you need exact words rather than general ideas.

items: Green plants make food by photosynthesis, using carbon dioxide, water and light energy.
Digestion breaks large food molecules into smaller ones that can be absorbed.
An element is a substance made of only one kind of atom, such as carbon or nitrogen.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Composition
| Nutrient | Elements present | Made up of | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| Carbohydrates | Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen (hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio 2 : 1, as in water) | Simple sugars joined together | Glucose, sucrose, starch, cellulose |
| Fats and oils | Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen (far less oxygen than in carbohydrates) | One glycerol joined to three fatty acids | Palm oil, groundnut oil, butter |
| Proteins | Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and often sulphur | Amino acids joined in long chains | Beans, egg white, fish, meat |

Fats are solid at room temperature while oils are liquid.

### Uses in the body
| Nutrient | Main uses |
|---|---|
| Carbohydrates | Main source of energy, stored as glycogen in the liver and muscles; cellulose forms plant cell walls |
| Fats and oils | Energy store (about twice as much energy per gram as carbohydrates); insulation under the skin; protection of organs; part of cell membranes; solvent for vitamins A, D, E and K |
| Proteins | Growth and repair of cells and tissues; making enzymes, antibodies and haemoglobin; energy only when other sources run short |

### Sources
Carbohydrates: cassava, yam, plantain, maize, rice. Fats and oils: palm oil, groundnuts, butter. Proteins: beans, fish, eggs, meat, groundnuts, soya.

A diet lacking protein, especially in a young child, leads to poor growth and the disease called kwashiorkor.

variantes.nom: Plants build proteins from different raw materials
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks why plants need minerals from the soil
variantes.contenu_markdown: Carbohydrates need only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen, which the plant gets from carbon dioxide and water. Proteins also need nitrogen, which the plant takes from the soil as nitrate ions through its roots. Without nitrates, a plant cannot make enough protein, so its growth is stunted and its leaves turn pale.

sections.enonce_markdown:
A young child is fed mostly on boiled cassava roots and very little else. The child grows slowly and has a swollen abdomen.

(a) Name the nutrient that is most likely lacking from the diet and the disease that results.
(b) Give two ways in which the body uses this nutrient.
(c) Suggest two foods that would improve the diet.

etapes.action: Identify what boiled cassava roots mainly supply.
etapes.justification: Cassava roots are rich in starch, which is a carbohydrate, and low in protein.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The diet gives energy but little protein.

etapes.action: Link the symptoms to the missing nutrient.
etapes.justification: Slow growth and a swollen abdomen are signs of protein deficiency in children.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Protein is the missing nutrient and the disease is kwashiorkor.

etapes.justification: The question asks how the body uses it, so give functions.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Proteins are needed for growth and repair of tissues and for making enzymes and antibodies.

etapes.justification: Foods containing amino acids correct the deficiency.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Beans and fish (eggs or groundnuts are also acceptable).

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) Protein; kwashiorkor. (b) Growth and repair of body tissues; making enzymes (or antibodies). (c) Beans and fish.

items.erreur_markdown: Carbohydrates are made of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen.
items.pourquoi_faux: Nitrogen is a feature of proteins. Carbohydrates contain only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen.
items.correction_markdown: Carbohydrates: C, H, O. Proteins: C, H, O, N and often S.

items.erreur_markdown: Fats are made of amino acids.
items.pourquoi_faux: Amino acids are the units of proteins. A fat molecule is made of glycerol and fatty acids.
items.correction_markdown: Fat: glycerol plus three fatty acids. Protein: amino acids.

items.erreur_markdown: The only product of photosynthesis is oxygen, which the plant uses up.
items.pourquoi_faux: Oxygen is a by-product that leaves the leaf. The food product is glucose, which is used or changed to other substances.
items.correction_markdown: Glucose is the food product and is used for respiration, stored as starch or changed to other substances; oxygen is released.

items.erreur_markdown: Proteins are used only for energy.
items.pourquoi_faux: The main uses of proteins are growth, repair and making enzymes; they supply energy only when carbohydrates and fats are short.
items.correction_markdown: Proteins are used for growth and repair, enzymes and antibodies, and for energy only when other sources run out.

items.enonce_markdown: State the chemical elements present in each of (a) carbohydrates, (b) fats, (c) proteins.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **Carbon, hydrogen and oxygen**.
(b) **Carbon, hydrogen and oxygen** (with a much smaller proportion of oxygen than in carbohydrates).
(c) **Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen**, and often sulphur.

items.enonce_markdown: Complete the table for garri, palm oil and beans: the main organic nutrient and one use of that nutrient in the body.
items.solution_markdown:
| Food | Main nutrient | One use in the body |
|---|---|---|
| Garri | **Carbohydrate** | Provides energy |
| Palm oil | **Fat (oil)** | Energy store, or insulation |
| Beans | **Protein** | Growth and repair |

items.enonce_markdown:
A potato plant has just made glucose in its leaves in bright sunlight.

(a) Describe four things that can happen to this glucose.
(b) Explain why the plant also needs nitrates from the soil to make proteins.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Award a mark for each of four points: it is used in respiration to release energy; it is changed to starch and stored in the tubers; it is changed to sucrose and moved in the phloem to growing parts; it is changed to cellulose for new cell walls (or to fats and oils).
(b) **Proteins contain nitrogen**, which glucose does not contain. The plant combines the glucose with nitrate ions absorbed by the roots to make amino acids, and these join to form proteins.

items_markdown: Carbohydrates contain carbon, hydrogen and oxygen; fats the same three elements; proteins also contain nitrogen.
Carbohydrates are made of sugar units, fats of glycerol and fatty acids, proteins of amino acids.
Carbohydrates give energy; fats store energy and insulate; proteins give growth, repair, enzymes and antibodies.
The main product of photosynthesis is glucose, which is used in respiration or changed to starch, sucrose, cellulose, fats or proteins.
Plants need nitrates from the soil to make proteins; lack of protein in a child causes kwashiorkor.
